claims.title: Monoikos named by Hecataeus
claims.summary: The Greek geographer Hecataeus of Miletus refers to Monoikos as a Ligurian town, the earliest known mention of the site that would become Monaco; later the Phocaeans of Massalia developed it as a port.

sources.label: A port during Greek then Roman antiquity

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-550bce-monoikos-named-by-hecataeus, claim TL:MCO:event:550bce:monoikos-named-by-hecataeus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The harbour at its height
claims.summary: The port of Monoikos, associated with the cult of Hercules, flourished as part of Mediterranean trade, as shown by coins and goods recovered from the harbour.

sources.label: A port during Greek then Roman antiquity

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-300bce-the-harbour-at-its-height, claim TL:MCO:event:300bce:the-harbour-at-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portus Herculis Monoeci under Rome
claims.summary: After Rome's conquest of the region the harbour became Portus Herculis Monoeci, a refuge on the route between Italy, Gaul and Hispania used by Roman expeditions.

sources.label: A port during Greek then Roman antiquity

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-137bce-portus-herculis-monoeci-under-rome, claim TL:MCO:event:137bce:portus-herculis-monoeci-under-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Caesar uses the port
claims.summary: Julius Caesar is recorded as having used the harbour of Monoeci around 50 BCE, a measure of its importance as a Roman anchorage on the Ligurian coast.

sources.label: A port during Greek then Roman antiquity

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-50bce-caesar-uses-the-port, claim TL:MCO:event:50bce:caesar-uses-the-port, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Genoa fortifies the Rock
claims.summary: Genoese Ghibellines under Fulco del Cassello began building a fortress of four towers on the Rock of Monaco, offering land and tax exemptions to draw settlers to the new stronghold.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1215-genoa-fortifies-the-rock, claim TL:MCO:event:1215:genoa-fortifies-the-rock, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Grimaldi seizes the Rock
claims.summary: François Grimaldi, called Malizia, took the fortress disguised as a Franciscan monk, beginning the Grimaldi presence in Monaco, an event commemorated by the armed monks of the princely coat of arms.

sources.label: Occupation of the Rocher by François Grimaldi

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1297-grimaldi-seizes-the-rock, claim TL:MCO:event:1297:grimaldi-seizes-the-rock, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Purchase of Menton
claims.summary: Charles I Grimaldi, regarded as the founder of the principality, enlarged the Grimaldi domain by purchasing the lordship of Menton, which remained Monégasque until 1861.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1346-purchase-of-menton, claim TL:MCO:event:1346:purchase-of-menton, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Purchase of Roquebrune
claims.summary: The Grimaldi added the lordship of Roquebrune to their possessions, completing the territory that, with Monaco and Menton, would define the principality for five centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1355-purchase-of-roquebrune, claim TL:MCO:event:1355:purchase-of-roquebrune, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Honoré II takes the title of Prince
claims.summary: Honoré II became the first Grimaldi to call himself Prince and Lord of Monaco, marking the principality's emergence as a sovereign state out of the medieval lordship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1612-honore-ii-takes-the-title-of-prince, claim TL:MCO:event:1612:honore-ii-takes-the-title-of-prince, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Péronne
claims.summary: Honoré II and Louis XIII signed the Treaty of Péronne, shifting Monaco from Spanish to French protection while recognising the principality's independence and the prince's sovereignty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1641-treaty-of-peronne, claim TL:MCO:event:1641:treaty-of-peronne, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French titles for the Grimaldi
claims.summary: Under the Péronne settlement the prince of Monaco received French titles and estates, including the duchy of Valentinois, binding the dynasty to the French crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1642-french-titles-for-the-grimaldi, claim TL:MCO:event:1642:french-titles-for-the-grimaldi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The fortress becomes a palace
claims.summary: Honoré I and Honoré II employed leading architects to transform the Genoese fortress into a princely residence, creating one of the most remarkable palaces of the seventeenth century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1685-the-fortress-becomes-a-palace, claim TL:MCO:event:1685:the-fortress-becomes-a-palace, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolutionary France annexes Monaco
claims.summary: Revolutionary France abolished the Grimaldi sovereignty and annexed the principality, expelling the dynasty and scattering the palace's art collections.

sources.label: Secession of Menton and Roquebrune (Treaty of 1861)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1793-revolutionary-france-annexes-monaco, claim TL:MCO:event:1793:revolutionary-france-annexes-monaco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Menton and Roquebrune secede
claims.summary: Amid the revolutions of 1848, Menton and Roquebrune declared themselves free towns, banished the prince and sought union with Sardinia, which then occupied them.

sources.label: Secession of Menton and Roquebrune (Treaty of 1861)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1848-menton-and-roquebrune-secede, claim TL:MCO:event:1848:menton-and-roquebrune-secede, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cession of Menton and Roquebrune
claims.summary: By the Franco-Monégasque Treaty, Prince Charles III ceded Menton and Roquebrune to France for four million francs; France recognised Monaco's sovereignty over its remaining territory.

sources.label: Secession of Menton and Roquebrune (Treaty of 1861)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1861-cession-of-menton-and-roquebrune, claim TL:MCO:event:1861:cession-of-menton-and-roquebrune, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Société des Bains de Mer
claims.summary: Charles III established the Société des Bains de Mer to develop a casino quarter, leasing the gambling monopoly to François Blanc, who had previously enriched the spa of Homburg.

sources.label: History of the company (Société des Bains de Mer)
sources.publisher: Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer

claims.title: Monte-Carlo named
claims.summary: Prince Charles III decreed that the new casino district be called Monte-Carlo in his honour; its gambling revenues rebuilt Monaco's finances and let the principality abolish direct taxation in 1869.

sources.label: History of the company (Société des Bains de Mer)
sources.publisher: Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1866-monte-carlo-named, claim TL:MCO:event:1866:monte-carlo-named, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Monaco's first constitution
claims.summary: Prince Albert I granted Monaco a constitution on 5 January 1911, ending absolute princely rule and beginning the principality's evolution into a constitutional state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1911-monaco-s-first-constitution, claim TL:MCO:event:1911:monaco-s-first-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Franco-Monégasque Treaty of 1918
claims.summary: Signed amid a succession crisis, the treaty aligned Monaco's policy with French interests and provided that the principality would fall under French protection should the Grimaldi line end; it was noted in the 1919 Treaty of Versailles.

sources.label: The history of Monaco's accession
sources.publisher: Permanent Representation of Monaco to the Council of Europe (gouv.mc)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1918-franco-monegasque-treaty-of-1918, claim TL:MCO:event:1918:franco-monegasque-treaty-of-1918, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rainier III marries Grace Kelly
claims.summary: Prince Rainier III married the American actress Grace Kelly, who became Princess Grace; their union brought the principality international glamour and helped drive its post-war revival.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1956-rainier-iii-marries-grace-kelly, claim TL:MCO:event:1956:rainier-iii-marries-grace-kelly, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 1962 constitution
claims.summary: Rainier III promulgated a new constitution that reduced the sovereign's powers, abolished capital punishment and granted women the right to vote.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Monaco: A rock above the sea held for seven centuries by one family, the longest-reigning dynasty in Europe.", terralore.co/country/MCO/chronicle#ev-1962-the-1962-constitution, claim TL:MCO:event:1962:the-1962-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Monaco joins the United Nations
claims.summary: Monaco was admitted as the 183rd member state of the United Nations, an unambiguous international recognition of its full sovereignty.

sources.label: United Nations Member States (Monaco admitted 28 May 1993)

claims.title: Treaty of 2002 guarantees independence
claims.summary: A new Franco-Monégasque treaty, with the revised constitution and succession law, ended the clause returning Monaco to France if the Grimaldi line failed, guaranteeing the principality's continued independence.

sources.label: The history of Monaco's accession
